subject: general
question: I bought two toy guns for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 8% and the second at a gain of 16%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first toy gun.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a "no profit, no loss" transaction, the absolute loss on one item exactly equals the absolute gain on the other.

Loss on 1st toy = Gain on 2nd toy ⇒ 8% of CP₁ = 16% of CP₂

⇒ CP₁ : CP₂ = 16 : 8 = 2 : 1

Total CP ratio parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts → ₹1200

⇒ 1 part → ₹400 ⇒ CP₁ (2 parts) = 2 × 400 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two toy guns = ₹1200

Loss on the first toy gun = 8%

Gain on the second toy gun = 16%

Overall transaction result = Neither loss nor gain

 
 CP of Toy 1 (2 parts)
 
 
 CP2 (1 part)

 

 Total Cost = ₹1200 (3 parts)

 -8% Loss
 +16% Gain
 Loss = Gain (8% of CP1 = 16% of CP2)

**Calculations:**

Let the cost price of the first toy gun be x.

⇒ The cost price of the second toy gun = (1200 − x)

⇒ Total loss on first toy = 8% of x = 0.08x

⇒ Total gain on second toy = 16% of (1200 − x) = 0.16 × (1200 − x)

Since the overall transaction has no loss or gain, total monetary loss equals total monetary gain:

⇒ 0.08x = 0.16 × (1200 − x)

Dividing both sides by 0.08:

⇒ x = 2 × (1200 − x)

⇒ x = 2400 − 2x

⇒ x + 2x = 2400

⇒ 3x = 2400

⇒ x = 2400 ÷ 3 = 800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Principle

When a transaction results in neither profit nor loss, the absolute monetary value of the gain on one item strictly balances the absolute monetary loss on the other: CP₁ × Loss% = CP₂ × Profit%.

Alligation in Profit & Loss

When two items are sold at different profit or loss percentages and combined for an overall percentage result, the alligation cross-difference method immediately provides the ratio of their Cost Prices (never Selling Prices).

Same Selling Price Condition

If two articles are sold at the same Selling Price (instead of same total Cost Price), one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, the entire transaction always results in an overall loss equal to (x² ÷ 100)%.
